# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 6 (Bu-Vb Ss6)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Kuṭikāra* ("Building a hut inappropriately") is the sixth training rule of the Saṅghādisesa category in the Pali *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates individual monastic dwellings, prescribing that whenever a bhikkhu constructs a hut by begging for materials, he must obtain formal approval from the Saṅgha regarding the building site, and the dwelling must not exceed specified maximum dimensions; breaching either of these stipulations incurs an offense entailing suspension (*saṅghādisesa*) [SuttaCentral]. The rule's canonical origin story incorporates the *Maṇikaṇṭha Jātaka*—found in slightly different form in the canonical Jātaka collection (Ja 253)—alongside an additional edifying tale aligned with the *Aṭṭhisenaka Jātaka* (Ja 403) and an apparent reference to Raṭṭhapāla of the *Raṭṭhapāla Sutta* (MN 82) [SuttaCentral].
Full parallels are widely attested across all major early Vinaya traditions, with corresponding rules and analyses preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions of the Dharmaguptaka, Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya traditions, as well as the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra* [SuttaCentral]. Machine text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus reveal extensive internal Pali sharing, particularly with the subsequent rule *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Saṅghādisesa 7* (exceeding 170,000 shared characters), Khandhaka procedures (notably Kd 11, Kd 13, Kd 15, and Kd 6), and post-canonical Vinaya literature including the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*, *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā*, and *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language text-reuse detected by DharmaNexus corroborates these textual relationships, aligning segments of the Pali text with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003) and *Vinayavastu* (D0001), as well as Sanskrit Vinaya witnesses including the *Prātimokṣasūtra* and *Śayanāsanavastu* [DharmaNexus].
